audience: Graduate scientists who want to distinguish a mathematical result from progress on its exposition.
assistance: AI drafted this public teaching synopsis, its renderings and its claim map. Human scientific and bilingual reader review are pending.

claims.quote: Every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part exactly 1/2. The zeros at negative even integers are called trivial.
claims.evidence: Andrew Sutherland, What was verified, item 1 and the definition of RiemannHypothesis. https://math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/

claims.quote: On 21 November 2026, the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative certified the formal statement and proof of the classical Riemann hypothesis.
claims.evidence: Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative, joint statement on 21 November 2026, including checks 1–4. https://leanprover-community.github.io/blog/posts/riemann-hypothesis/

claims.quote: Rubinstein’s working guide reduces its central inequality to thirteen hypotheses and leaves those hypotheses unproved within the guide.
claims.evidence: Michael Rubinstein, The proof explained for the Riemann zeta function, version 2, 22 November 2026. https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/~mrubinst/alpoge_claude_grh/

en.text: The Riemann zeta function has zeros at the negative even integers. These are called trivial zeros. The theorem says that every nontrivial zero has real part exactly 1/2.
On 21 November 2026, the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative certified both the formal statement of this classical result and its proof.
Writing down how the argument works is a further task. Rubinstein’s guide reduces its central inequality to thirteen hypotheses and leaves their proofs open within the guide.

es.text: La función zeta de Riemann tiene ceros en los enteros pares negativos. Se llaman ceros triviales. El teorema afirma que cada cero no trivial tiene parte real exactamente igual a 1/2.
El 21 de noviembre de 2026, la Lean FRO y la Mathlib Initiative certificaron el enunciado formal de esta hipótesis clásica y su demostración.
Explicar cómo funciona el argumento requiere otro paso. La guía de Rubinstein reduce su desigualdad central a trece hipótesis y deja pendientes sus demostraciones en ese texto.
